# LocalDate

A date (and time) in the reader's own time zone and language, in a `<time>` that carries the exact instant. Only the browser knows the reader's time zone, so the server writes the instant in UTC, hydration repeats it so the markup matches, and the browser then shows the local one. A date then changes only when the instant falls near midnight, but a time (`time`, `datetime`) changes for every reader outside UTC, so the server's text names the zone ("9:30 AM UTC") until the browser takes over. A calendar date with no time ("2026-06-01") is the same day for everyone and is written the same on the server and in the browser.

```tsx
import { LocalDate } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/local-date/local-date";
```

## Example

```tsx
<LocalDate value={note.updatedAt} format="datetime" />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `RelativeTime` instead for "3 days ago", and `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in your own text for a date inside a sentence you build.

## Props

Type: `LocalDateProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only. Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `format` | `"date" \| "month" \| "datetime" \| "time"` | `"date"` | `date` "Jun 1, 2026", `month` "Jun 2026", `datetime` "Jun 1, 2026, 9:30 AM", `time` "9:30 AM". |
| `locale` | `Intl.LocalesArgument` | the reader's | The language and region to write it in. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLTimeElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `value` (required) | `Date \| string \| number` |  | The instant: a `Date`, an ISO string or a timestamp in milliseconds. A calendar date with no time ("2026-06-01", or "2026-06" with `format="month"`) is that day for every reader and is never moved into a time zone. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `children`: Not a prop. The text is the date; there are no children.
- `date`: Not a prop. The instant is `value`: `<LocalDate value={note.createdAt} />`.
- `dateTime`: Not a prop. The instant is `value`; the `<time>` gets its `dateTime` from it.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
